eliyah_rabbah.en: [Levush] Because of a non-Jew, etc. For example, a nation that does not permit light to be kindled on its festival except in its temple. Rashi and Ran in Bameh Madlikin explain "an evil spirit" as a condition in which darkness comforts the person. Rambam explains that "evil spirit" refers broadly to illnesses called melancholy in Arabic, in which the patient departs from the balanced human disposition during episodes of confusion; this occurs frequently among people of certain temperaments. Bartenura calls them people of black bile. Perishah writes that some people imagine frightening things if a lamp burns while they sleep, leading to mental disturbance. He says he found no explicit source, but I found it in Abudarham.

וכתבו התוס' דף ל"א ודף צ"ד כצ"ל כלומר הכא שמכוין לכיבוי כו' ר"ל שם גבי סגירת דלת דהמלאכה היא הצידה והוא אינו מכוין לציד' כלל כ"א לסגור זה מקרי פ"ר אבל כיבוי דהמלאכ' היא כביה והוא ג"כ מתכוין נכיבוי אלא שאינו מתכוין לתכליתה דהא א"צ לגוף הכיבוי אלא שחס על הנר וכדומה ולכן מיקרי מלאכה שאצ"ל. אולם לדעת הרמב"ם דפוסק במלאכ' שאצ"ל כר"י דחייב וכן בפ"ר קי"ל דחייב אפי' לר"ש וא"צ לחלק בין מלאכ' שאצ"ל ובין פ"ר כ"א לענין קריאת השם דהא חייב בשניהם א"ש אבל לדעת הטור דפסק כר"ש דמלאכ' שאינה צ"ל פטור. ובפ"ר חייב לפי סברת הרר"א אדרב' איפכא מסתברא דיותר ראוי לחייב במלאכ' שאצ"ל דעל כל פנים נתכוין למלאכה מלחייב בפ"ר דלא נתכוין כלל למלאכ' וכן קשה לר"ש גופי' דפוטר במלאכה שאצ"ל ומחייב בפ"ר. וצ"ל דבשבת דמלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה א"כ יש לומר במלאכה שאצ"ל דנתכוין למלאכ' ולא נתכוין לתכלית' הרי מחשבתו הוציאה מכלל מלאכ' מה שאין כן בפ"ר דלא נחכוין כלל למלאכה ולא הוציא מחשבתו מכלל מלאכה (וע' סי' רס"ח ס"ק ג' בשם הרא"ש לענין ברכה קצת דמיון):
ול"נ דלר"א חובל חייב כו' דאיתא בשבת דף ק"ו ע"א תני ר"א קמיה דר"י כל המקלקלין פטורים חוץ מחובל ומבעיר א"ל ר"י פוק תני לברא כי אינו משנה ואת"ל משנה חובל בצריך הדם לכלבו ומבעיר בצריך לאפרו והוי מתקן ופריך הש"ס לר"א והתנן כל המקלקלין פטורין משמע אפי' חובל ומבעיר ומשני הא ר"י והא ר"ש ופי' התוס' דר"י ס"ל מקלקל אפי בחובל ומבעיר פטור ור"ש ס"ל חייב כדדריש שם מקרא והקשו התוס' לר"ש דמחייב בחובל ומבעיר אפי' אצ"ל לכלבו ולאפרו ואמאי ניהו דבהני תרי אפי' מקלקל חייב מ"מ הא הוי מלאכה שאצ"ל דפטור לר"ש ומצינו כמה סוגיין דלר"ש אפי' מקלקל בחבלה בעינן צריך לגופה ותי' דמשכחת לה שצ"ל ואפ"ה הוי מקלקל כגון שחבל וצריך לכלבו והבעיר וצריך לאפרו וצריכה לגופה לפי מחשבתו אח"ז נודע שהם אסורי הנאה ואסור ליתן לכלב או ליהנות מן האפר נמצא למפרע הוי מקלקל מ"מ צריכה לגופה מקרי דהא לפי מחשבתו היה צ"ל אבל במס' ב"ק תי' התוס' דמיירי אפי' א"צ לכלבו ולאפרו ואפ"ה לר"ש חייב דכמו דבעלמא מקלקל פטור מ"מ בחובל ומבעיר חייב ה"ה דחייב אע"ג דא"צ לגופיה אע"ג דבעלמא פטור כן ס"ל לר"א והני סוגיא דמוכח דגם בחובל ומבעיר בעי שיהיה מלאכה שצ"ל אתיין כר' יוחנן הרי דלדברי התוס' בב"ק לר"א אליבא דר"ש בחובל אפי' א"צ לדם והוי מקלקל וגם א"צ לגופה מ"מ חייב וי"ל דגם הטור ס"ל כן לכן אע"ג דפסק כר"ש דמלאכה שאצ"ל פטור מ"מ בחובל בחברו בשבת פטור דק"ל בדרבה מיניה דהא בחובל אפי' א"צ לגופה חייב:

(ג) And Tosafot wrote on daf 31 and daf 94, as it should read — meaning here that he intends for extinguishing, etc. — meaning there regarding closing a door, where the melacha is trapping and he does not intend trapping at all but only to close — this is called psik reisha; but extinguishing, where the melacha is extinguishing and he also intends extinguishing, only he does not intend it for its own sake, for he does not need the extinguishing itself but pities the candle and the like — therefore it is called melacha she'eina tzricha legufa. However, per the Rambam who rules melacha she'eina tzricha legufa like Rabbenu Yehudah that one is liable, and so too for psik reisha we hold liable even per R' Shimon, and one need not distinguish between melacha she'eina tzricha legufa and psik reisha except regarding reading the Shem — for one is liable in both — it would seem; but per the Tur who ruled like R' Shimon that melacha she'eina tzricha legufa is exempt, and for psik reisha liable per the view of the Rosh — on the contrary it is more reasonable to obligate in melacha she'eina tzricha legufa, for in any case he intended melacha, than to obligate in psik reisha where he did not intend melacha at all; and so too R' Shimon himself is difficult, who exempts melacha she'eina tzricha legufa and obligates psik reisha. And one must say that on Shabbat, where melacha requires intent, one may say in melacha she'eina tzricha legufa that he intended melacha but did not intend its purpose — behold his intent removed it from the category of melacha, which is not so in psik reisha where he did not intend melacha at all and his intent did not remove it from melacha (and see siman 268, note 3, in the name of the Rosh regarding blessing — somewhat similar).

(ד) And in my humble opinion, for R' Eliezer one who injures is liable, etc. — for it is stated in Shabbat 106a: R' Eliezer taught before R' Yehudah: all who damage are exempt except one who injures and one who kindles. R' Yehudah said to him: go teach outside, for he does not change the Mishnah. And if you say he changes — injuring where he needs the blood for his dog, and kindling where he needs its ash, and it is repair — the Gemara challenges R' Eliezer, and we learn: all who damage are exempt — implying even injuring and kindling; and it answers: this is R' Yehudah and this is R' Shimon. And Tosafot explain: R' Yehudah holds that even damaging in injuring and kindling is exempt, and R' Shimon holds liable as he expounded from Scripture there. And Tosafot challenged R' Shimon — why is he liable in injuring and kindling even she'eina tzricha legufa for his dog and for its ash? Nevertheless in these two, even when damaging he is liable; nevertheless it is melacha she'eina tzricha legufa that is exempt per R' Shimon, and we find several sugyot that for R' Shimon even damaging in injury requires tzricha legufa, and one must say that you find it where it is nevertheless damaging, such as he injured and needs it for his dog, and he kindled and needs its ash, and it is needed for its own sake per his later thought — it becomes known they are items forbidden for benefit and forbidden to give to a dog or benefit from the ash — it turns out retroactively he was damaging; nevertheless it is called needed for its own sake, for per his thought it was needed; but in Bava Kamma Tosafot explain it deals even where he does not need it for his dog or its ash, and nevertheless per R' Shimon he is liable — just as generally damaging is exempt, nevertheless in injuring and kindling he is liable — so too here he is liable even though not needed for its own sake, even though generally exempt — so holds R' Eliezer, and these sugyot prove that even in injuring and kindling one requires melacha tzricha legufa — they come according to R' Yochanan; behold per Tosafot in Bava Kamma, for R' Eliezer according to R' Shimon in injury even without needing blood and it is damaging and also not needed for its own sake — nevertheless he is liable. And one may say the Tur also holds thus — therefore even though he ruled like R' Shimon that melacha she'eina tzricha legufa is exempt, nevertheless for injuring one's fellow on Shabbat he is exempt from payment, for we learn from it, for in injury even without needing for its own sake he is liable.

(ה) And in Yesh Nofesh, etc. — in a quarrelsome manner if his intent, etc., as it should read — and therefore the Tur's ruling in Choshen Mishpat is well explained, that one who injures his fellow on Shabbat is exempt from payment, for we learn from it — for even though he holds melacha she'eina tzricha legufa is exempt, nevertheless if his intent was that blood would come out (so that he would weaken and the other would overpower him — so too there in Yesh Nofesh) it is needed for its own sake.

And their dispute stems from what is stated in Shabbat 105b: one who tears in his anger on Shabbat is liable, and we conclude it is according to R' Yochanan, who holds melacha she'eina tzricha legufa is liable; and it challenges: nevertheless is he not damaging? And it answers that it is repair, for he satisfies his inclination; and it challenges: it was taught — one who tears his garments in anger should be in your eyes like one who worships idols; and it answers: for example, he did it to instill fear in his household. And Rashi explains the questioner's difficulty: since it is like idol worship, how can it be called repair? And so explains the Raavad, and it answers: for example he did it to instill fear — it is not like idol worship, and therefore it is repair; but if he intended a transgression it is damaging. But the Rambam explains the Gemara's question was: since it is like idol worship, the baraita should conclude and this thing is forbidden even on a weekday. And it answers: for example he did it, etc. — he did not commit a prohibition, but in any case even if he committed a transgression in his act, nevertheless it is called repair in that he satisfied his inclination, and he is liable regarding Shabbat and exempt even per R' Yehudah — meaning who holds she'eina tzricha legufa is liable — nevertheless he is exempt because he is damaging.

yad_ephraim.he: במג"א ס"ק א' וביש"ש בב"ק פ"ח סימן ך"ב דהחובל דרך מריבה ודעתו שיצא ממנו דם הוי צריך לגופא כצ"ל. ועיין ביש"ש דאיתא שם ודעתו שיצא ממנו דם ויחלוש כנגדו אז הוי שפיר צריך לגופו. וא"ל מנא ידעינן אם דעתי לכך וי"ל דמודה ואעפ"י שאין אדם משים עצמו רשע לומר שחלל שבת מ"מ בנידון זה כבר נעשה רשע שהכה חבירו ואיתרע חזקת כשרותו וא"ל דהמחזיק יקבל בהיסת שדעתו היה להוציא דם ממנו דא"כ דומה לנשבע להרע מאחר דאין אדם משים עצמו רשע אף שכבר נעשה רשע בהרמת יד מ"מ איך יוסף בשבועה שהרשיע יותר וחייב מיתה. ואף שאיתרע חזקת כשרותו ועומד לכך ס"ס הוא נשבע על רשעתו ודומה לשבועת שוא וגם י"ל דסתמא כו' עכ"ל. ומ"ש המג"א דהוי חילול ש"ש כתב מדעתו להסביר סברת היש"ש בקצרה. ומ"מ הדמיון לנשבע להרע הוא תמוה ולענ"ד בלא"ה לק"מ שהרי הנחבל טוענו שמא והחובל טוען ברי וא"כ אין כאן אפי' שבועת היסת:
yad_ephraim.en: In Maga sak 1 and Bishash in Bk 18, sign 22 Dahovel through a quarrel and his opinion that blood came out of him, he should have his body as 21. And look at the Yishash Daita there and his opinion that blood came out of him and became weak against him, then he is benign, he should have his body. And El Mana Yadeinan if my opinion is that, and El Damoda, and if a person does not call himself an evil person to say that he violated Shabbat MM in this matter, he has already become an evil person who struck his friend and questioned his kosher status. If his presumption of kosherness is delayed and he stands for it, he swears about his wickedness and it is similar to a false oath, and also 11 Destma, 11 Akal. And the M.S. Maga Dahui Hilul Shash wrote out of his mind to briefly explain the meaning of the Shish. And from M.M. the similitude of swearing to evil is puzzling, and the OT in the L.A. to KM, since the one who was guilty claimed that the one who was guilty was claiming that he was guilty, and yet there is no Efi' of the swearing oath here:
